cefrAlignment: Matches B2 (CEFR CV: can follow the essentials of an extended discussion and identify speakers' viewpoints and changes of position): 220–260-word two-speaker discussions with partial agreement, doubt and explicit changes of mind.
examFidelity: IELTS Part 3 matching (5 items, 7 options, 2 unused) and 'who says it? A/B/C' match the real task, and the two-question TOEFL Conversations fit the exams.ts description; every item follows the audio order.
fixes: Practice 1: Daniel's second 'Same here' (reacting to Maya's 'Even my flatmate could follow it') was ambiguous and repeated his earlier line; changed it to 'I found it really clear too' so that agreement on 'easy to understand' is clear.
openConcerns: 'Who says it?' items depend on learners telling the two TTS voices apart; names are said in the dialogue, but a specialist should check that the browser voices for each pair are clearly different.
learnerOutcome: A learner can track two speakers through a discussion, tell agreement from partial agreement and doubt, and use a speaker's final view to answer IELTS Part 3 matching and TOEFL opinion questions.
